correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(b>1\), the exact positive radial root is strictly increasing in nearest-antipodal-center distance. Polar Voronoi integration gives the circular-gap identity; \(F_b''(s)>0\) establishes Jensen rigidity. Uniform angles give a Dirichlet spacing vector, with \(\mathbb E S_3=48\pi^3/((m+1)(m+2))\) and a Taylor remainder satisfying \(\mathbb E R_m^2=O_b(m^{-8})\). The exact normalized cubic-gap variance is \(72(m-1)(5m+11)/((m+1)^2(m+2)^2(m+3)(m+4)(m+5))\); multiplying by \(m^5\) gives the limit \(360\). The exponential delta-method influence variable \(E^3-18E+12\) has variance \(360\), proving the Gaussian coefficient \(40\alpha^2\pi^6\). The bundled verifier completed 60 independently integrated configurations and 16 moment/inequality checks. Numerical checks do not substitute for the analytic proof. The edge \(b=1\) is excluded.

originality.rationale: The integrated theorem characterizes a singular uniform-circumference center law and gives an exact finite-\(m\) expectation, a parameter-independent factor-six design gap, and the specific \(m^{-5}\) area variance constant \(40\alpha^2\pi^6\). The closest fully inspected primary work establishes deterministic circumscribed disc-polygon symmetry, assumes bounded continuous center densities in ambient space, or samples points from a convex-body interior. Its statements do not imply this boundary-angle Dirichlet functional or its constants. Classical circular-spacing central limit methods are acknowledged. Residual historical equivalence is stated explicitly, not ruled out by unsuccessful searches.
residual_risks: Earlier boundary-sampled random disc-polygon work under alternate terminology, or a general smooth-spacing functional CLT instantiated with the same radius law, could imply or match this calculation; no categorical historical independence or exhaustive coverage claim is made.

The deterministic existence of a symmetric minimizer overlaps classical Dowker-type convex-body approximation results; only the complete analytic gap law and combined statistical refinements are argued not to be explicitly covered.

Some classical results on random polygons inscribed in circles have cubic-gap CLTs with analogous universal variance mechanisms; their distinct straight-edge area objective is not identical to the present fixed-b disk-intersection statistic.

value.rationale: The exact area gap formula and its strict convexity classify all minimizers for the natural unit-circle center constraint. The expectation and the \(m^{-5}\) area variance and Gaussian limit quantitatively compare deterministic and random boundary placement; the sharp factor-six excess is an intrinsic scale-free efficiency law. This motivated full-family result is not an arbitrary finite slice, a table lookup, or a routine normalization check; the explicit constants support reproducible benchmarks for disk-intersection sampling.
